boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Redbird rituals, songs, ceremonies, and recurring events that connect Illinois State students and alumni.

cards.title: Every Graduate Gets the Microphone Moment
cards.subtitle: A name-by-name commencement custom dating to Illinois State’s earliest graduating class
cards.notes: Listen for every graduate’s name and watch each person cross the stage; ceremonies are organized by college in December and May.
cards.short_summary: Illinois State centers commencement on individual recognition rather than a featured speaker.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois State identifies commencement as its oldest tradition, dating to 1860, and says every graduate’s name is called individually before they cross the stage.
cards.access_notes: University ceremonies are held in December and May at Braden Auditorium and CEFCU Arena; participation and guest access depend on commencement arrangements.

cards.title: The Parade That Outlived the Hobo Era
cards.subtitle: A Redbird procession whose official Homecoming story began in 1921
cards.notes: Choose a public parade-route viewing point and look for student groups, alumni, and Reggie; confirm the current route before attending.
cards.short_summary: A century-old parade carries Illinois State’s fall reunion through Normal.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois State calls Homecoming its second-oldest tradition and says the first official celebration in 1921 included an alumni parade from Old Main to the football field.
cards.access_notes: The parade occurs during the annual fall Homecoming celebration; consult the current Homecoming schedule and route before visiting.

cards.title: One Ringer for Every Year
cards.subtitle: Illinois State’s birthday ceremony built around a replica of the Old Main Bell
cards.notes: Attend the Founding ceremony and count the succession of bell ringers, with one person selected for every year of university history.
cards.short_summary: Illinois State marks its birthday by turning institutional age into a sequence of bell strikes.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois State says its Founding bell-ringing ceremony continues with individuals selected for every year the university has existed; a replica Old Main bell joined the ceremony in 2010.
cards.access_notes: The ceremonial ringing is associated with the university’s February Founding observance; verify the current event schedule and venue.

cards.title: Touch the Bronze Bird Before Battle
cards.subtitle: The student-athlete ritual centered on Illinois State’s Battle Bird sculpture
cards.notes: Photograph the bronze Battle Bird outside competition time; leave the formal pregame touch to Illinois State coaches and student-athletes.
cards.short_summary: A sculpture unveiled in 2000 anchors a ritual linking generations of Redbird athletes.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois State documents that every coach and student-athlete touches the Battle Bird before each game as a gesture connecting Redbird athletes past and present.
cards.access_notes: The pregame touch is performed by coaches and student-athletes; public viewing depends on the sport, venue access, and event admission.

cards.title: Win First, Then Lead the Chorus
cards.subtitle: A Redbird victory ritual using a melody first written in 1932
cards.notes: After a Redbird win, stay for the student-athlete-led fight song and follow the crowd’s first-stanza cue without entering team areas.
cards.short_summary: The team and home crowd turn each victory into a shared rendition of the ISU fight song.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois State says student-athletes traditionally lead the home crowd in singing the fight song after a win; the song was written in 1932 and later received new lyrics.
cards.access_notes: This ritual follows Redbird victories at home athletic events; venue admission and access rules vary by sport.

cards.title: The Quad Becomes One Giant Sign-Up Sheet
cards.subtitle: Illinois State’s fall organization fair, held annually since 1989
cards.notes: Walk the Quad booth by booth, note groups you want to revisit, and ask student representatives about meeting commitments before joining.
cards.short_summary: Hundreds of booths transform the Quad into a live index of campus involvement.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois State says Festival ISU began in 1989, has been held on the Quad every fall since, and features nearly 300 registered student organizations.
cards.access_notes: Festival ISU is a fall event on the Quad; consult the current university event listing for its date, weather plan, and visitor details.

cards.title: From Passages to a Week of Redbird Arrivals
cards.subtitle: A campus welcome tradition whose earliest organized efforts date to 1955
cards.notes: Use the week’s tours to locate Milner Library, Bone Student Center, and academic buildings, then select social or service events that fit.
cards.short_summary: A former boxed-lunch welcome has evolved into tours, gatherings, concerts, and service opportunities.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois State traces campus welcoming efforts to 1955 and says Welcome Week, formerly called Passages, now helps new and returning students acclimate through tours and events.
cards.access_notes: Welcome Week takes place around the start of the academic year; individual programs may be limited to students or require registration.

cards.title: A School Hymn Distilled into Four-Part Harmony
cards.subtitle: The Redbird alma mater performed from a hymn composed during 1913–14
cards.notes: Listen to the Big Red Marching Machine’s four-part arrangement before an event, then follow the printed words when the campus sings together.
cards.short_summary: Illinois State’s alma mater preserves a compact portion of an older school hymn.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois State says its Alma Mater is a shortened version of the school hymn composed by Gussie Schneider during the 1913–14 school year and documents a four-part band performance.
cards.access_notes: The tradition appears at university performances and ceremonies; access depends on the host event’s admission rules.

cards.title: A College Circus That Is Greek by Name Only
cards.subtitle: Illinois State’s student circus tradition, organized in 1926
cards.notes: Watch for tumbling, aerial, balance, and ensemble acts at the annual show; use official performance guidance for any audience participation.
cards.short_summary: Redbird performers sustain a collegiate circus tradition with roots in campus athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois State says Gamma Phi Circus dates to 1926, is not part of the Greek system, and is the oldest collegiate circus in the United States.
cards.source_title: Gamma Phi Circus | Traditions | Illinois State
cards.access_notes: Annual performances are traditionally staged in April; current dates, venue rules, and ticket requirements should be checked with Gamma Phi Circus.

cards.title: Friday Has an Official Color
cards.subtitle: The weekly Redbird custom introduced by a campus-community pride committee
cards.notes: Add a red layer or existing Redbird item on Friday; participation is the color cue itself, so no special purchase is necessary.
cards.short_summary: Students, employees, alumni, and friends use Friday clothing as a recurring campus signal.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois State documents a Friday tradition in which students, faculty, staff, alumni, and friends wear red or Redbird gear; the idea began in the early 2000s.
cards.source_title: Wear Red on Friday | Traditions | Illinois State
cards.access_notes: This weekly tradition can be observed anywhere on campus or in the community; specific events may have their own access rules.
